abstract: Recent advances in spatial omics have enabled tissue atlases spanning serial sections, donors, and experimental technologies. Aligning these datasets is essential for comparing spatial organization, reconstructing three-dimensional tissue architecture, and registering sections to a common coordinate framework. However, systematic comparisons of alignment accuracy, computational efficiency, and usability remain limited. Here, we benchmarked 15 tissue alignment and registration algorithms using experimental and simulated spatial transcriptomics datasets across pairwise alignment, three-dimensional reconstruction, cross-resolution alignment, and atlas registration tasks. We assessed spatial-domain and cell-type correspondence, spatial gene-expression similarity, computational scalability, and usability. Simulated datasets with known spatial coordinates additionally enabled direct evaluation of geometric accuracy and reconstruction stability. No single method performed best across all settings: performance depended on the task, spatial resolution, and tissue characteristics, and strong pairwise alignment did not necessarily translate into reliable three-dimensional reconstruction. Evaluation metrics captured complementary aspects of alignment quality, highlighting the importance of using multiple criteria for comprehensive assessment. These findings provide practical guidance for method selection and identify priorities for improving the accuracy, scalability, and accessibility of spatial omics alignment.
